\lby{Baumg\"artel--Jurke--Lled\'o, ``Twisted duality of the CAR-algebra'' (\texttt{refs/BJL\_twisted\_duality\_math-ph-0204029.pdf}),
 Theorem~7.1 (PDF p.~27): $\mathcal M(\mathfrak q)'=\widetilde Z\mathcal M(\mathfrak q^\perp)\widetilde Z^*$ for every
 basis projection and every closed $\Gamma$-invariant $\mathfrak q$, applied with the hypotheses checked in the box
 below; the inclusion $\cM'\subseteq Z\cF(I')Z^*$ (the \emph{duality} half) is what is used.  (Replaces the earlier
 citation of Foit 1983, whose screenshot was NOT OBTAINED.)}
\begin{citedbox}{BJL 2002, Theorem 7.1 (twisted duality)}
(i) Verbatim: ``Let $(\mathfrak h,\Gamma)$ be a Hilbert space with anti-unitary involution $\Gamma$, $P$ \emph{any}
basis projection and $\mathfrak q$ \emph{any} closed $\Gamma$-invariant subspace in $\mathfrak h$'' (p.~26, start of
\S7); ``7.1 Theorem (Twisted Duality) \dots\ Then $\mathcal M(\mathfrak q)'=\widetilde Z\,\mathcal M(\mathfrak q^\perp)\,
\widetilde Z^*$'' (p.~27).  Definitions: basis projection $P+\Gamma P\Gamma=\one$, Fock state $\omega_P(a(f)^*a(f))=0$
for $Pf=f$ (p.~4, eq.~(2)); $\mathcal M(\mathfrak q):=\{a(q)\mid q\in\mathfrak q\}''$ (p.~7, eq.~(7));
$\widetilde Z:=\frac1{1+i}(\one+iZ)$, $Z$ the implementer of the even--odd automorphism (p.~5 before eq.~(4); p.~8,
eq.~(8)); the complex case: $\mathfrak h:=H\oplus H$, $\Gamma:=\begin{pmatrix}0&\gamma\\\gamma&0\end{pmatrix}$,
diagonal basis projection $\mathrm{diag}(\mathcal P,\gamma\mathcal P^\perp\gamma)$ (p.~25).
\shot[0.8\textwidth]{r1_BJL_sec7_setup.png}\shot[0.8\textwidth]{r1_BJL_thm71.png}
\shot[0.8\textwidth]{r1_BJL_basisproj.png}\shot[0.8\textwidth]{r1_BJL_Mq.png}
\shot[0.8\textwidth]{r1_BJL_twist.png}\shot[0.8\textwidth]{r1_BJL_complex.png}
(iv) Use and (v) hypotheses, one by one.  $H=L^2(\mathbb R)$, $\gamma$ complex conjugation, $\mathfrak h=H\oplus H$,
$\Gamma(f\oplus g)=\gamma g\oplus\gamma f$: an anti-unitary involution.  Self-dual field
$a(f\oplus g):=a(f)+a^*(\gamma g)$ with (C2)'s $a$: antilinear, $a(F)^*=a(\Gamma F)$, and
$\{a(F),a(G)^*\}=\ip FG$ (from the CAR of (C2) and $\ip{\gamma g'}{\gamma g}=\ip g{g'}$): BJL Thm.~2.1 (i)--(iii).
$\mathfrak P:=\mathrm{diag}(\Pm,\gamma\Pp\gamma)$ (BJL's $\mathcal P=\Pm$): $\Gamma\mathfrak P\Gamma=
\mathrm{diag}(\Pp,\gamma\Pm\gamma)$, so $\mathfrak P+\Gamma\mathfrak P\Gamma=\one$.  For $\mathfrak PF=F$,
$F=f\oplus g$: $\omega(a^*(f)a(f))=\ip f{\Pp f}=0$ and $\omega(a(\gamma g)a^*(\gamma g))=\ip{\gamma g}{\Pm\gamma g}=0$
by \eqref{eq:qf} ($\gamma g\in\Pp H$), the cross terms vanish (gauge invariance of the quasi-free $\omega$), so
$\omega=\omega_{\mathfrak P}$ on the field algebra, and the Fock representation of (C2) with its cyclic $\Om$ is the GNS
representation of $\omega_{\mathfrak P}$, unitarily equivalent to BJL's with $\Om\mapsto\Om$.
$\mathfrak q:=L^2(I)\oplus L^2(I)$ is closed and $\Gamma$-invariant, $\mathcal M(\mathfrak q)=\CAR(L^2(I))''=\cM$, and
$\mathfrak q^\perp=L^2(I')\oplus L^2(I')$ because $\mathbb R\setminus I=[1,\infty)$ differs from $I'$ by a null set,
so $\mathcal M(\mathfrak q^\perp)=\cF(I')$.  Twist: $Z$ and $V$ both implement the grading; BJL's $Z$ is the second
quantisation of the Bogoliubov unitary $-1$ (\emph{paraphrase} of p.~5; its source [4] is NOT OBTAINED), which fixes
$\Om$, as $V$ does, so $Z=V$ on the dense set $\CAR(H)\Om$.  The sign is in any case immaterial: replacing $Z$ by
$-Z$ replaces $\widetilde Z$ by $-i\widetilde Z^*$, and $\widetilde Z^*\cN\widetilde Z=\widetilde Z(Z\cN Z)\widetilde Z^*
=\widetilde Z\cN\widetilde Z^*$ for $\cN=\cF(I')$ ($\widetilde Z^2=Z$, $Z\cN Z=\cN$).  Verdict: hypotheses met.
\end{citedbox}
